Subject: Acme Finance: post-discovery ops qualification & tech asks

Thanks for taking the time earlier, Sarah and Tom — good call. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can loop in engineering and procurement: 

Summary (from our call)
- Goal: embed document summarization + QA + short-form generation into payroll support flows and an internal analytics pipeline.
- Traffic expectation: bursty daytime traffic with heavy end-of-month spikes (payroll cutoff).
- Must-have: predictable latency (~300ms p50 for chat-style queries), VPC connectivity, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Open technical/ops questions we need to lock down before sizing Dedicated capacity:
1) Typical request size (tokens): can you share average and 95th percentile tokens per request for summarization + QA?
2) Concurrent users and acceptable queueing: expected concurrent sessions during peak and how long requests can wait before timing out (SLO for tail latency).
3) Embeddings/reranker usage: will embeddings be generated in real-time per request or in a nightly batch? Any existing vector DB (Milvus/FAISS)?
4) Structured output / tool calling: do you need Redwood tool-calling (e.g., external DB lookups) or strict JSON schema outputs? Provide 1–2 example outputs.
5) Auth/network: will you use API keys or SSO (SAML/OIDC) + VPC peering? Procurement also asked about KMS/HSM support for keys.

Attachments: I uploaded Acme_requirements_v1.pdf and the call recording; I also attached a first-pass mutual_action_plan.xlsx with milestones.

Next steps (owners)
- Sarah/Tom: please answer the five bullets above and drop any sizing docs (Sarah mentioned an internal throughput report).
- Marissa (cc): can you prepare a short Dedicated sizing draft and an autoscaling recommendation based on their answers?
- Aditya (cc): will review commercial guardrails once we have the sizing.

Can we target a short tech sync next Tue (06/23) with Marissa and one of your infra folks? If that works, send an invite and the best contact for SSO/network.

Thanks — Laura

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and I've attached a brief internal traffic snapshot.

Answers to your bullets:
1) Tokens: average ~420 tokens for summarization requests; 95th ~1,800 tokens for longer docs. QA queries are generally 160–240 tokens.
2) Concurrency: during normal days ~60 concurrent sessions; month-end peaks up to ~650 concurrent. Our current frontend times out at 45s but we'd like to keep user-facing waits under 10s.
3) Embeddings: hybrid approach — nightly batch for full-document vectors, plus real-time embeddings for short queries (<300 tokens). We use an in-house FAISS cluster.
4) Structured output: yes, we need strict JSON responses for the automated downstream ingestion (example: {"summary":"...","key_dates":["2026-05-01"],"confidence":0.89}). We also plan a small set of tool calls to our internal payroll microservice (auth via OAuth2).
5) Auth/network: SSO (SAML) is preferred for admin flows; runtime will use API keys for service-to-service. We require VPC peering and HSM-backed key management for secrets.

Attaching: acme_traffic_snapshot_June.pdf

I'll loop Tom for a tech contact — Tom, can you add the infra lead who should join the Tue sync?

Best,
Sarah

On Sat, Jun 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@acme-finance.com> wrote:
> Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and I've attached a brief internal traffic snapshot.
> 
> Answers to your bullets:
> 1) Tokens: average ~420 tokens for summarization requests; 95th ~1,800 tokens for longer docs.

Thanks for the details, Sarah — super helpful. Based on what you've shared, a first-pass Dedicated sizing + autoscaling approach we recommend: 

Preliminary sizing assumptions (please confirm)
- Baseline qps: assume 60 sustained QPS (average daytime) and 650 concurrent sessions at peak.
- Token mix: weighted average tokens/request ~600 (mix of QA & summarization).
- Latency targets: 300ms p50, 1s p90 (for generation-only paths); overall end-to-end target under 10s for user flows when including downstream tool calls.

Suggested Dedicated configuration
- Node type: GPU instances with 80GB memory (model-dependent); start with 4 nodes for baseline, scale to 16 nodes for peak bursts.
- Concurrency limits: cap concurrent inference threads per node based on model footprint; we usually tune to achieve target latency with a 5–10% headroom.
- Autoscaling policy: hybrid — keep a baseline of 3 nodes (min), scale by RPS with a 60s evaluation window, and an emergency queue-based scale-up trigger for spike detection (queue length > 200 requests triggers +2 nodes).
- Warm KV cache persistence between requests to reduce cold-start token costs for repeated doc contexts.

Auth / network notes
- We support SAML/IdP for admin and API keys for runtime tokens; for VPC peering we recommend a private endpoint with TLS and mutual auth. HSM/KMS integration is supported for customer-managed keys.

Embeddings/reranker notes
- Nightly batch embeddings are straightforward to handle off-cluster or on lower-cost compute; real-time embeddings should be routed to a smaller pool optimized for short-sequence models.
- For reranking we recommend a two-stage flow: candidate generation from lightweight model (lower-cost) followed by a reranker on Dedicated for highest-quality top-N scoring.

Structured output & tool calling
- We can enforce JSON schema validation at the runtime and return structured errors if validation fails.
- Tool calls: we can add a secure webhook connector with OAuth2 client credentials flow to call your payroll microservice; we recommend adding a 3–5s soft timeout for non-blocking UX.

Action items
- Sarah/Tom: please confirm the throughput numbers and whether 650 concurrent is sustained or a short-lived peak.
- Sarah: please share an infra contact to join Tue 06/23 10:00am PT.
- Laura/Aditya: advise on commercial SLAs for warm-standby nodes and pricing cadence; I can produce a sizing worksheet and an ops runbook draft before the call.

I'll prepare the sizing workbook and a short runbook (queue thresholds, health checks, rollout steps) and upload prior to Tue.

Thanks — Marissa
